title: الطلاقة — مراجعة ومشروع ختاميّ
subtitle: Integration: everything, together
intro: Fluency is not one more structure. It is the ability to reach for the right one without stopping to think. This final unit mixes everything you have studied, on purpose, without labels — because that is how English actually arrives.الطلاقة ليست تركيباً إضافيّاً، بل القدرة على بلوغ التركيب الصحيح دون توقّفٍ للتفكير. وهذه الوحدة الختاميّة تخلط كلّ ما درسته عمداً وبلا عناوين — لأنّ هكذا تصلك الإنجليزيّة فعلاً.
goals: I can switch between structures without planning them
I can hold a real conversation at natural American speed
I can write a structured 250-word piece at B2 level

blocks.title: Your grammar map — level one
blocks.html:
1 present simple ↔ continuous · 2 past simple ↔ continuous · 3 present perfect + for/since · 4 will / going to / present continuous · 5 comparatives and superlatives · 6 should / must / have to
7 prepositions and quantifiers · 8 present perfect ↔ past simple · 9 infinitive ↔ gerund · 10 the passive (simple) · 11 first and second conditional · 12 reported speech + relative clauses

If any line here makes you hesitate, open that unit again before the test on day seven.هذه خريطة المستوى الأوّل. إن تردّدت عند أيّ سطر، فافتح تلك الوحدة قبل اختبار اليوم السابع.

blocks.title: Your grammar map — level two
blocks.html:
13 present perfect continuous + discourse markers · 14 the passive across all tenses · 15 past perfect and narrative tenses · 16 third and mixed conditionals · 17 full reported speech · 18 modals of deduction
19 the causative (have/get sth done) · 20 inversion and cleft sentences · 21 reduced relatives and participles · 22 hedging · 23 the unreal past (wish / if only / I'd rather)

These eleven are what separate B1 from B2. Nothing above this level is more useful than using these accurately.هذه الإحدى عشرة هي ما يفصل B1 عن B2. ولا شيء فوق هذا المستوى أنفع من استعمالها بدقّة.

blocks.title: The six errors that survive everything
blocks.html:
Even advanced Arabic speakers keep these. Check every piece of writing for them:

1. informations / evidences / researches / advices → all uncountable
2. He said me → He told me
3. If I would have known → If I had known
4. discuss about / explain me → discuss X / explain X to me
5. I am agree → I agree
6. since two years → for two years

Six lines. Fixing them permanently raises your perceived level more than any new grammar will.ستّة أخطاء تنجو من كلّ شيء عند العرب المتقدّمين. وتصحيحها نهائيّاً يرفع مستواك الظاهر أكثر من أيّ نحوٍ جديد.

blocks.title: The fluency habit
blocks.html:
Accuracy is built by correction. Fluency is built by not stopping.

Practise this: speak for sixty seconds about anything, and forbid yourself from going back to fix a mistake. Then speak about the same thing again. The second run is always better, and the improvement comes from the fact that you did not stop the first time.

Both skills are necessary. Use writing for accuracy and speaking for fluency. Trying to do both at once is why people freeze.الدقّة تُبنى بالتصحيح، والطلاقة تُبنى بعدم التوقّف. استعمل الكتابة للدقّة والكلام للطلاقة — ومحاولة الجمع بينهما في آنٍ واحد هي سبب التجمّد.

days.title: Reading: what to do after the course
days.subtitle: نصّ + استنتاج المعنى من السياق

blocks.title: The Plateau Is the Point
blocks.en:
Everyone who reaches B2 in a second language discovers the same unpleasant fact: progress stops feeling like progress. The first year is dramatic — you go from silence to sentences. The fourth year is invisible, because the remaining gaps are not gaps in grammar. They are gaps in exposure.

This is why the advice that works at B2 is so different from the advice that works at A2. Having finished a structured course, the useful next step is not another structured course. It is volume: hours of input slightly above your level, repeated, in areas you would consume anyway. A person who watches forty hours of one American series with English subtitles will improve more than one who studies forty hours of vocabulary lists, because the series teaches collocation, rhythm and register, which lists cannot.

It is worth noting that the plateau feels like failure and is not. Comprehension deepens before production does; you understand jokes months before you can make them. If you had recorded yourself a year ago, the difference would be obvious. You didn't, so it isn't.

The one habit that separates people who reach C1 from people who stay at B2 is unglamorous: they produce language regularly, in writing, and someone or something corrects it. Everything else — apps, films, podcasts, conversation — builds the input. Correction is what converts it.
blocks.ar:
كلّ من يبلغ مستوى B2 في لغةٍ ثانية يكتشف الحقيقة غير السارّة نفسها: يتوقّف التقدّم عن الإحساس بأنّه تقدّم. فالسنة الأولى مذهلة — تنتقل من الصمت إلى الجمل. والسنة الرابعة غير مرئيّة، لأنّ الفجوات المتبقّية ليست فجواتٍ في النحو بل في التعرّض.

ولهذا فالنصيحة التي تنفع في B2 مختلفةٌ جدّاً عن التي تنفع في A2. فبعد أن أنهيتَ دورةً منظّمة، لا تكون الخطوة التالية المفيدة دورةً منظّمةً أخرى، بل الكمّ: ساعاتٌ من المُدخل الأعلى قليلاً من مستواك، مكرّراً، في مجالاتٍ كنتَ ستستهلكها أصلاً. فمن يشاهد أربعين ساعةً من مسلسلٍ أمريكيٍّ واحد بترجمةٍ إنجليزيّة سيتحسّن أكثر ممّن يدرس أربعين ساعةً من قوائم المفردات، لأنّ المسلسل يعلّم التلازم اللفظيّ والإيقاع والمستوى اللغويّ، وهي ما لا تستطيع القوائم تعليمه.

ويجدر بالملاحظة أنّ الهضبة تبدو فشلاً وليست كذلك. فالفهم يتعمّق قبل الإنتاج؛ إذ تفهم النكات بأشهرٍ قبل أن تستطيع صنعها. ولو كنتَ سجّلت نفسك قبل عام لكان الفرق بيّناً. لكنّك لم تفعل، فلم يكن بيّناً.

والعادة الوحيدة التي تفصل من يبلغون C1 عمّن يبقون في B2 غير برّاقة: إنّهم يُنتجون اللغة بانتظام، كتابةً، ويصحّحها لهم أحدٌ أو شيءٌ ما. وكلّ ما عداها — التطبيقات والأفلام والبودكاست والمحادثة — يبني المُدخل. والتصحيح هو ما يحوّله.

blocks.title: One idea, five registers
blocks.html:
«لا أستطيع فعل ذلك»:

No way. — with friends
I can't, sorry. — neutral spoken
I'm afraid that won't be possible. — professional
Unfortunately, we are unable to accommodate that request. — formal written
Regrettably, the proposal falls outside the scope of this agreement. — legal / institutional

Choosing the wrong register is a bigger error than choosing the wrong tense. A native speaker forgives a grammar slip instantly and remembers a register mistake for weeks.اختيار المستوى اللغويّ الخاطئ خطأٌ أكبر من اختيار الزمن الخاطئ. يغفر الناطق الأصليّ زلّة النحو فوراً ويتذكّر زلّة المستوى أسابيع.

blocks.title: The twelve phrases that do the most work
blocks.html:
If you learn only twelve things from this course, learn these:

To be fair, … · That said, … · The thing is, …
I see it slightly differently. · My concern would be that …
I'd rather you didn't. · I'm not comfortable with that.
In hindsight, … · It remains unclear whether …
What I'm saying is … · Let me come back to you on that.
For what it's worth, …

Every one of them buys you a second to think, and none of them sounds like a learner.كلّ واحدةٍ منها تمنحك ثانيةً للتفكير، ولا تبدو أيٌّ منها لغة متعلّم.

blocks.title: 🚫 قائمة الأخطاء الكاملة — راجعها قبل كلّ نصّ تكتبه
blocks.html:
الأسماء غير المعدودة: information · evidence · research · advice · feedback · knowledge · progress · equipment

الأفعال: discuss X (لا about) · explain X to me · tell someone / say something · I agree (لا am agree) · It depends on · afford X (لا to)

الأزمنة: for two years (لا since) · If I had known (لا would have) · can't have (لا mustn't have) · I wish I had (لا would have)

الصفات: I'm bored ≠ I'm boring · prices are high ≠ expensive · historical ≠ historic

التعابير: لا تكتب do the needful ولا revert back ولا according to me ولا In nowadays.هذه قائمة المراجعة النهائيّة. مرّرها على كلّ نصٍّ تكتبه بالإنجليزيّة لسنةٍ كاملة، ثمّ لن تحتاجها.

blocks.title: The final project
blocks.prompt:
Write 250 words on this question: What has changed in how you use English over the last year, and what will you do next?

Structure it in four paragraphs:
• 1 — Where you started. Narrative tenses, past perfect.
• 2 — What changed and why. Present perfect / present perfect continuous, one causative.
• 3 — What you would do differently. One third or mixed conditional, one wish or I'd rather.
• 4 — The plan. Hedged predictions, one cleft or inversion for emphasis.

Required across the whole piece: eight structures from the grammar map, six words or phrases from the course, and zero items from the error list.اكتب ٢٥٠ كلمة في أربع فقرات كما هو موضّح: البداية، ما تغيّر، ما كنتَ ستفعله على نحوٍ مختلف، والخطّة. مطلوبٌ ثمانية تراكيب من خريطة النحو، وستّ كلماتٍ من الدورة، وصفرٌ من قائمة الأخطاء.
phrases: A year ago I had barely …
By the time I started …, I had already …
I had my writing corrected by …
If I had started …, I would be … now
I wish I had … / I'd rather I had …
It is not X but Y that has made the difference.
Never have I … as consistently as …
It is likely that … / It remains unclear whether …
Over the next six months, I intend to …
blocks.model:
A year ago I had barely used English outside a classroom. I could read a technical page slowly, and I had memorised more grammar than I had ever produced. By the time I started this course, I had already abandoned two apps, both for the same reason: they tested what I knew rather than what I could do.

What has changed is not my grammar. I have been listening to American speech almost daily, and I have had my writing corrected every week, which turned out to matter more than either activity alone. The listening built recognition; the correction converted it into something I could use.

If I had started with films instead of word lists, I would be further ahead now — though I would probably have a weaker grasp of tenses, so perhaps the order was not wrong. I wish I had recorded myself in the first week. I'd rather have the evidence than the impression.

It is not vocabulary but rhythm that has made the largest difference, and never have I noticed that as clearly as when I stopped translating in my head. Over the next six months, I intend to write two hundred words a week and have them corrected, watch one series with English subtitles rather than five, and speak for a minute a day without stopping to fix myself.

It remains unclear whether that is enough for C1. It is, however, the only plan I have tested that survived a full year.
blocks.modelAr:
قبل عام لم أكن قد استعملتُ الإنجليزيّة خارج قاعة الدرس إلّا بالكاد. كنتُ أقرأ صفحةً تقنيّة ببطء، وكنتُ قد حفظتُ من النحو أكثر ممّا أنتجتُ يوماً. وبحلول بدئي هذه الدورة كنتُ قد تخلّيتُ عن تطبيقين، وكلاهما للسبب نفسه: كانا يختبران ما أعرفه لا ما أستطيع فعله.

وما تغيّر ليس نحوي. فقد ظللتُ أستمع إلى الكلام الأمريكيّ يوميّاً تقريباً، وجعلتُ من يصحّح كتابتي أسبوعيّاً، وتبيّن أنّ هذا أهمّ من أيٍّ من النشاطين وحده. فالاستماع بنى التعرّف، والتصحيح حوّله إلى شيءٍ أستطيع استعماله.

ولو بدأتُ بالأفلام بدل قوائم الكلمات لكنتُ أبعد شوطاً الآن — مع أنّ قبضتي على الأزمنة كانت ستكون أضعف على الأرجح، فربّما لم يكن الترتيب خاطئاً. وليتني سجّلتُ نفسي في الأسبوع الأوّل؛ فأنا أفضّل أن أملك الدليل لا الانطباع.

وليست المفردات بل الإيقاع هو ما أحدث الفارق الأكبر، ولم ألحظ ذلك بهذا الوضوح قطّ كما لحظته حين توقّفتُ عن الترجمة في رأسي. وفي الأشهر الستّة القادمة أنوي أن أكتب مئتي كلمةٍ أسبوعيّاً وأجعل من يصحّحها، وأن أشاهد مسلسلاً واحداً بترجمةٍ إنجليزيّة لا خمسة، وأن أتكلّم دقيقةً يوميّاً دون توقّفٍ لتصحيح نفسي.

ويبقى من غير الواضح إن كان ذلك كافياً لبلوغ C1. لكنّه الخطّة الوحيدة التي جرّبتها وصمدت عاماً كاملاً.

qs.q: By the time the auditors arrived, the files ___ .
qs.why: مجهولٌ في الماضي التامّ: حدثٌ سبق حدثاً ماضياً.

qs.q: If they had diversified, they ___ exposed now.
The office was empty. They ___ left early.

Which is correctly hedged for a report?

opts: the clauses to add in March

qs.q: She asked me ___ I had read it.
a: if
whether

qs.q: It's high time we ___ (write) this down.
a: wrote

qs.q: I've been waiting ___ nine o'clock.
a: since

qs.q: صحّح: He said me that he will discuss about it.
a: He told me that he would discuss it
He told me he would discuss it
qs.why: tell + شخص، وwill ← would، وdiscuss بلا about.

qs.q: صحّح: If I would have known, I wouldn't of signed.
a: If I had known, I wouldn't have signed
If I'd known, I wouldn't have signed
qs.why: لا would في شقّ if، وwould have لا would of.

qs.q: صحّح: There are many researches and evidences about this.
a: There is a lot of research and evidence about this
There is considerable research and evidence on this

qs.q: صحّح: I am agree, but the prices are very expensive.
a: I agree, but the prices are very high
I agree, but prices are high
qs.why: agree فعل، والسعر مرتفع لا غالٍ.

qs.a: It was the timing that cost them the deal

qs.say: I wuda told ya if I'd nown
a: I would have told you if I had known
I would have told you if I'd known

qs.say: He musta bin waydin the hole time
a: He must have been waiting the whole time
qs.why: must have been + flap T في waiting.

qs.say: Wudaya wan me ta do abowdit?
a: What do you want me to do about it?
What do you want me to do about it
qs.why: what do you ← وودَيَ، وabout it ← أباودِت.
